label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.69), depression scores (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.75), and anxiety scores (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.16) are all in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional difficulties. Despite advanced educational attainment, heavy digital engagement does not appear to buffer against psychological distress, and may coincide with social isolation and mood difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Elevated loneliness consistent with perceived social disconnection
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology across PHQ-9 items
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most pronounced of the three distress indicators
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional burden
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of multiple psychological stressors in a high-functioning demographic group

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With mean scores near the floor on all three psychological distress measures (UCLA-8 loneliness ≈ 0.75, PHQ-9 depression ≈ 0.35, GAD-7 anxiety ≈ 0.02), these individuals appear to be functioning well across emotional and social dimensions. They constitute a moderately sized group (n = 116) characterized by psychological resilience and stability.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen/social-media use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores suggesting strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology, well below clinical thresholds
Near-zero anxiety levels indicating effective emotional regulation
Moderate daily screen or social-media use (1–3 hours), suggesting balanced digital engagement
Higher educational attainment potentially linked to greater access to coping resources
tone: Stable, socially connected, and psychologically resilient
